question: Should outbound DM recipient authorization be added as Slack-specific channel config or as a generic outbound message policy that Slack participates in?
rationale: Both paths can address the report, but they create different public config, upgrade, and security semantics, and the repository guidance sets a high bar for new config and one-off channel policy.

options.title: Generic outbound policy
options.body: Add a transport-aware outbound recipient policy that Slack can enforce while leaving room for other message channels to share the same authorization model.

options.title: Slack-specific allowlist
options.body: Add `allowTo`/`dmAllowTo` only to Slack config, keeping the change smaller but creating channel-specific policy surface that may need later consolidation.

options.title: No new config yet
options.body: Keep the issue open for security design until maintainers decide whether current agent instructions and operator controls are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Generic outbound policy
recommendation.body: Add a transport-aware outbound recipient policy that Slack can enforce while leaving room for other message channels to share the same authorization model.

likelyOwner.reason: Kevin Lin has the strongest current code-history signal across the Slack config/send and outbound runtime paths that would need to change.
